mainEntity.name: What is lead management for a small business?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is the routine that takes a customer from first contact to a finished job and a review: one place where every lead lands, a prompt reply, a note of the source, follow-up until there is an answer, and a review request after the work.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a CRM to manage leads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not to begin. A spreadsheet or shared notes page with a date, contact details, service, source, status and next step covers the basics. Move to dedicated software only when the habits are in place and the list has outgrown the spreadsheet.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which marketing channel brings the best leads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Record the source of every lead and what happened to it. Once you have enough notes, compare each source by how many leads it sent, how many you reached and how many became jobs. Asking "How did you hear about us?" on every first contact is the simplest way to start.

mainEntity.name: Can I offer a discount in exchange for a Google review?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says offering incentives such as discounts or free goods in exchange for reviews is "fake & misleading content" and "strictly prohibited." You can ask customers to leave a review using a Google link or QR code, as long as you offer nothing in return.

mainEntity.name: Can I use WhatsApp for customer leads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Treat WhatsApp as one more channel that feeds your single lead list. The WhatsApp Business app is intended for one phone number, so decide who holds the phone, and set up a greeting and an away message that match what you can actually deliver.
